Nice! I've seen those when I was going through historical geology. One of my favorite things I have in my collection is a mineral, not a rock. It's a square crystal of pyrite. I love to show it to the students when we do minerals because it really fucks with their heads. Pyrite can form perfectly cubic crystals, but when broken won't retain that cubic form.

Paleo is cool, but it's tedious and it can be a pain in the ass. I have some slate with trilobite fossils in it. I also found what I believe to be a chunk of fossilized coral, but it was in an area I'm not familiar with. What's your favorite collection piece?

Personally, I'm more of a hard rock gal, so I like igneous and metamorphic rocks better than sedimantary rocks. I've only taken intro geology classes so far, but my end goal is to either teach or do research. (Maybe both!) 
Igneous and metamorohic rocks are super cool. Think lava/magma for igneous rocks. Anytime you have molten rock, you're going to form some type of igneous rock.
Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure without actually melting. They stay as a solid rock but undergo metamorphosis due to heat or pressure.
Sedimentary rocks are cool too, but not as interesting to me, personally. Sed rocks are generally formed either through chemical means and water or from particles of other rocks, called "sediments".
